BLD-lock_after_guard.content:
The lock SHALL be taken at process start, immediately after the workspace root is resolved and its sentinel,
`photos-00-workspace-guard`, is verified.
sections: Shared — how this build does it
BLD-lock_after_guard.title: The lock follows the workspace guard

BLD-lock_owner_record.content:
The lock SHALL record the identity of the process that owns it and the time it started, so that a lock whose owner is
gone can be told from one whose owner is running.
sections: Shared — how this build does it
BLD-lock_owner_record.title: The lock records its owner

BLD-one_snapshot_mechanism.content:
The three phases SHALL take their snapshots through one mechanism — prep §14.3, geotag §29 and merge §10.3 invoke it,
and none redefines it.
sections: Shared — how this build does it
BLD-one_snapshot_mechanism.title: One snapshot mechanism for every phase

BLD-phase_commands.content:
The phases SHALL be the commands `photos-cartographer prep`, `geotag` and `merge` — named in the specs, and in their
records, `photos-1-prep`, `photos-2-geotag` and `photos-3-merge`.
sections: Shared — how this build does it
BLD-phase_commands.title: The phases are three commands

BLD-phases_inside_lock.content:
Each phase's `plan`, `dry-run` and `execute` SHALL run with the lock taken at start already held; none SHALL take it
again or scope it on its own (prep §14, geotag §29).
sections: Shared — how this build does it
BLD-phases_inside_lock.title: The phases run inside the run's lock

BLD-snapshot_is_zfs.content:
The snapshot SHALL be a ZFS snapshot, configured by the `zfs` block of the workspace configuration,
`photos-00-config.json`; with no `zfs` block, or one not enabled, none is taken. Its name SHALL carry the plan id.
`snapshots_required` decides what a failed snapshot means: true, the run aborts before its first change; false, or the
block not configured, it proceeds without one.
sections: Shared — how this build does it
BLD-snapshot_is_zfs.title: The snapshot is a ZFS snapshot, configured by the `zfs` block

DEF-geotag.content:
**Geotag**, the second phase, resolves each photo to its true time, inferring and correcting each camera's clock
offset; places the photos that carry no position along the recorded tracks; and renames each by its corrected local
time.
DEF-geotag.title: Geotag

DEF-library.content:
The **library** is the permanent, curated collection the media ends in — outside every workspace, and written only by
merge.
DEF-library.title: The library

DEF-merge.content:
**Merge**, the third phase, runs after a workspace has been geotagged and finalized: it moves the finalized media,
sorted by destination, into the library — never renaming or overwriting anything already there — and then seals the
workspace.
DEF-merge.title: Merge

DEF-prep.content:
**Prep**, the first phase, takes an unorganized dump and makes it a clean working set: it consolidates the dump,
normalizes extensions, sets duplicates aside (recoverably, never deleting), organizes the media by date, and hands
geotag what it found.
DEF-prep.title: Prep

DEF-workspace.content:
A **workspace** is the transient place one ingest happens in: a dump of media enters it, the phases work on it in
turn, and merge empties it into the library. Every run acts on exactly one workspace.
DEF-workspace.title: The workspace

INV-one_run_at_a_time.content:
At most one cartographer run SHALL act on a workspace at any time — whatever the commands: two runs of one phase, runs
of two phases, a merge, a finalize, or a quarantine prune.
INV-one_run_at_a_time.title: One run at a time

RAT-lock_and_revalidation.content:
This whole-run lock is independent of, and stricter than, the dependency-revalidation discipline: revalidation guards
against *stale* inputs across separate runs, while the lock guarantees runs never overlap in the first place.
RAT-lock_and_revalidation.title: The lock and revalidation guard different things

RAT-one_filesystem_specific_part.content:
The mechanism is named for ZFS because that is the reference implementation, but it is deliberately the *only* part
of the pipeline that touches a specific filesystem feature, and it is optional; everything else is filesystem-agnostic.
RAT-one_filesystem_specific_part.title: Why the snapshot alone may touch the filesystem

RAT-one_snapshot_mechanism.content: Each phase that mutates uses the same mechanism so the phases behave identically and cannot diverge.
RAT-one_snapshot_mechanism.title: One mechanism, so the phases cannot diverge

RAT-planning_inside_lock.content:
Planning is non-mutating, but it must still not run concurrently: a plan computed against a workspace another process
is reading or mutating is untrustworthy, so planning is inside the lock too.
RAT-planning_inside_lock.title: A plan made beside another run cannot be trusted

RAT-snapshot_is_extra.content:
**Snapshots are an optional extra safety layer, not a requirement.** The pipeline operates fully and safely without
them: correctness and recoverability rest on the journal, recoverable quarantine, no-clobber operations, and
filesystem-as-truth reconciliation. Snapshots add a clean-slate rollback path on top of those for operators whose
filesystem supports it; they are not the basis of the safety model.
RAT-snapshot_is_extra.title: A snapshot is an extra layer, not the safety model

RUL-every_command_locks.content:
A workspace SHALL have exactly one lock, shared by every command. Every command that reads or changes the workspace
SHALL hold it while it does.
RUL-every_command_locks.title: One lock, taken by every command

RUL-filesystem_agnostic.content:
Nothing in cartographer but the snapshot SHALL depend on a particular filesystem's features; and cartographer SHALL run
fully on a filesystem that has none.
RUL-filesystem_agnostic.omit_reason: a design constraint over the whole code; the gap audit (backlog item 2) checks it
RUL-filesystem_agnostic.title: Only the snapshot depends on the filesystem

RUL-lock_before_reading.content:
A run SHALL hold the lock before it reads any of the workspace's content — before it plans, scans, fingerprints,
reads metadata, dry-runs or executes. Planning changes nothing, and is inside the lock all the same.
RUL-lock_before_reading.title: The lock comes before anything is read

RUL-lock_fail_fast.content:
A run that finds the workspace locked SHALL NOT wait for it. It SHALL stop at once, saying the workspace is locked by a
run in progress, having scanned, planned and changed nothing — and having produced no plan, no dry-run report and no
artifact.
RUL-lock_fail_fast.title: A locked workspace is refused at once

RUL-lock_released_on_any_end.content: A run SHALL release the lock when it ends, whether it succeeds or fails.
RUL-lock_released_on_any_end.title: The lock is released however the run ends

RUL-lock_through_the_run.content:
A run SHALL hold the lock until it ends — through planning, dry run, execution, and every record and artifact it
writes — and SHALL release it then. The lock SHALL NOT outlive its run: between runs, the workspace is unlocked.
RUL-lock_through_the_run.title: The lock lasts the whole run, and no longer

RUL-merge_snapshots_library.content: Prep's and geotag's snapshot SHALL cover the workspace; merge's SHALL cover the library, where its changes land.
RUL-merge_snapshots_library.omit_reason: carried by merge's own snapshot items, when merge is converted
RUL-merge_snapshots_library.title: Merge snapshots the library

RUL-required_snapshot_or_nothing.content: When the configuration requires snapshots, a run that cannot take one SHALL stop before it changes anything.
RUL-required_snapshot_or_nothing.title: A required snapshot that fails stops the run

RUL-snapshot_off_by_default.content: Snapshots SHALL be off unless the workspace's configuration turns them on.
RUL-snapshot_off_by_default.title: No snapshot unless configured

RUL-snapshot_optional.content:
A phase that changes files MAY first take a snapshot of what it is about to change, from which the whole change can be
rolled back. Cartographer SHALL be complete and safe without one: no guarantee SHALL depend on a snapshot having been
taken.
RUL-snapshot_optional.title: A snapshot is optional, and nothing rests on it

RUL-snapshot_per_plan.content: Each snapshot SHALL be identifiable by the plan whose changes it precedes.
RUL-snapshot_per_plan.title: A snapshot names its plan

RUL-snapshot_timing.content:
A snapshot SHALL be taken after the plan has been validated against its dependencies and the lock is held, and before
the plan's first change.
RUL-snapshot_timing.title: When a snapshot is taken

RUL-stale_lock_recovered.content:
A lock left behind by a run that died SHALL be recognisable as stale, and recoverable, so that a crash never leaves a
workspace locked for good.
RUL-stale_lock_recovered.title: A stale lock is recognised and recovered

RUL-stale_takeover_conservative.content:
A stale lock SHALL be taken over only when its owner is provably gone. A lock whose owner may still be running SHALL be
left alone.
RUL-stale_takeover_conservative.title: Only a dead owner's lock is taken over

RUL-unrequired_snapshot_proceeds.content:
When snapshots are not required, or not configured, a run SHALL proceed without one. Its safety then rests, as it
always does, on the journal, the recoverable quarantine, never overwriting, and the filesystem as the truth.
RUL-unrequired_snapshot_proceeds.title: Without a required snapshot, the run goes on

TST-cli-locked_workspace_failfast_produc.title: Lock contention is fail-fast and pre-mutation: a `plan` that can't take the workspace lock produces NO plan artifact and NO journal — the run never got past lock acquisition.

TST-lock-cross_process_exclusion_and_own.title: test cross process exclusion and owner report

arch.description: Mapping of uml key to uml content.

constraints.description: List of constraint names, which are defined for this need.

constraints_error.description: An error message set if any constraint failed, and `error_message` field is set in config.

constraints_passed.description: True if all constraints passed, False if any failed, None if not yet checked.

constraints_results.description: Mapping of constraint name, to check name, to result, None if not yet checked.

content.description: The main content of the need.

docname.description: Name of the document where the need is defined (None if external).

doctype.description: The markup type of the content, denoted by the suffix of the source file, e.g. '.rst'.

external_css.description: CSS class name, added to the external reference.

external_url.description: URL of the need, if it is an external need.

has_dead_links.description: True if any links reference need ids that are not found in the need list.

has_forbidden_dead_links.description: True if any links reference need ids that are not found in the need list, and the link type does not allow dead links.

is_external.description: If true, no node is created and need is referencing external url.

is_import.description: If true, the need was derived from an import.

is_modified.description: Whether the need was modified by needextend.

jinja_content.description: Whether the content was pre-processed by jinja.

layout.description: Key of the layout, which is used to render the need.

lineno.description: Line number where the need is defined (None if external).

parts.description: Mapping of parts, a.k.a. sub-needs, IDs to data that overrides the need's data

post_template.description: The template key, if the post_content was created from a jinja template.

pre_template.description: The template key, if the pre_content was created from a jinja template.

signature.description: Derived from a docutils desc_name node.

style.description: Comma-separated list of CSS classes (all appended by `needs_style_`).

template.description: The template key, if the content was created from a jinja template.
